question: What is the main goal of occupational health services?

options.B: Punishing employees who break safety rules
options.C: Reducing company expenses on worker salaries
options.D: Promoting worker well-being and preventing illness

explanation: You got this! Occupational health is all about keeping workers safe, healthy, and happy both physically and mentally. Great job! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h1)

question: How do occupational health programs differ from regular hospital care?

options.A: They only handle severe physical trauma and surgeries
options.B: They focus heavily on prevention and work environments
options.C: They ignore mental health and focus strictly on machinery
options.D: They are managed exclusively by financial auditors

explanation: While hospitals treat people after they fall sick, occupational health steps in early to make the workplace itself safe so illnesses never happen in the first place. Makes total sense, right? [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of a biological workplace hazard?
explanation: Biological hazards come from living things like germs, bacteria, and viruses (such as Hepatitis B) that can affect healthcare workers and others. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h2)

question: A data entry worker has severe lower back pain and wrist stiffness from a poorly adjusted desk. What type of hazard is this?
explanation: Ergonomic hazards happen when body posture, tools, or workstations don't fit the worker properly, leading to strain over time. Keep up the momentum! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h2)

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) ranked as the least effective way to control hazards?

options.A: It depends on human behavior and can easily fail or be worn incorrectly
options.B: It is always too expensive for companies to purchase in bulk
options.C: It completely removes the hazard from the physical environment
options.D: It increases the physical speed at which employees perform tasks

explanation: PPE is super important, but it's a last line of defense because if a worker forgets to wear it or wears it wrongly, they are still exposed to danger! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h3)

question: What control measure involves replacing a toxic chemical with a harmless water-based cleaner?
explanation: Think of 'substitution' like substituting a player on a football pitch—you take out the dangerous chemical and put in a safer one to do the same job! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of a pre-placement medical examination?

options.A: To determine the final retirement pension of the employee
options.B: To establish a baseline health status before job exposure begins
options.C: To diagnose casual community infections like malaria
options.D: To punish workers who have past medical conditions

explanation: A pre-placement check gives us a clear picture of a worker's health before they start a new job, so we can track and protect their health later on. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h4)

question: When is a return-to-work medical examination performed?

options.A: Before a new worker signs their initial employment contract
options.B: Every month as a routine check for all factory staff members
options.C: After an employee recovers from an illness or injury and prepares to resume duties
options.D: Immediately after a major chemical spill occurs on site

explanation: Spot on! This check ensures the worker is fully ready to return or tells us if they need lighter duties to avoid getting hurt again. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h4)

question: What is the very first critical step after an injury happens at work?

options.A: Administering prompt first aid and stabilizing the victim
options.B: Suspending the supervisor in charge of the department
options.C: Filing insurance paperwork with government regulators
options.D: Interviewing witnesses about company safety policies

explanation: As a nurse, saving lives and giving first aid always comes first before any paperwork or investigations. You're thinking like a true nurse! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h5)

question: Why is it important to investigate the root cause of a workplace accident?

options.A: To avoid paying workers' compensation claims to injured staff
options.B: To satisfy legal requirements without making actual workplace changes
options.C: To find an individual employee to blame and dismiss immediately
options.D: To prevent the same incident from happening again by fixing the underlying flaw

explanation: Finding the root cause isn't about witch-hunting; it's about fixing the system so that exact accident never happens to anyone else. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h5)

question: Which of these best describes a key clinical duty of an occupational health nurse?

options.A: Treating minor workplace injuries and managing chronic health checks
options.B: Designing factory buildings and heavy industrial machinery
options.C: Negotiating labor union contracts with company executives
options.D: Setting company stock prices and managing corporate budgets

explanation: As an occupational health nurse, you provide direct care by treating small injuries, giving first aid, and helping staff manage long-term health issues. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h6)

question: Why is patient confidentiality especially important for an occupational health nurse?

options.A: It encourages workers to seek help for personal or health issues without fear of job loss
options.B: It stops employees from talking to each other during working hours
options.C: It allows the company to hide safety violations from the public
options.D: It prevents government regulatory bodies from inspecting the workplace

explanation: Trust is everything! When workers know their medical secrets are safe with you, they will freely report symptoms and get help early. Brilliant work today! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h6)
